To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the four subtests (grammar, vocabulary, listening, and translation) were all highly reliable and valid when based on total scores; (2) the four subtest scores correlated moderately with each other; (3) the grammar and vocabulary subtests were highly reliable and valid; (4) the grammar subtest had the highest correlation with the GPA criterion, whereas the translation subtest had the lowest; (5) the translation subtest was the least reliable and valid; and
grammar is the most reliable and valid subtest when based on the total test score, and that translation is the least reliable and least valid subtest when using the same criterion.
the four components, grammar, listening, reading, and translation, are not equivalent with respect to reliability, validity, and unique variance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and validation of the four components of English as a Second Language, namely grammar, reading, listening comprehension, and translation.
the validation of four areas of competence in English as a foreign language: listening comprehension, grammar, vocabulary, and translation.
the identification and composition of the major areas of EFL competence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the four components of the test are all valid, but that the relative importance of each varies depending on the criterion used.
, although grammar was the most important component in terms of its contribution to the total score and its reliability, it was the least important in terms of its validity.
the four components of the English language test are not equally reliable and valid and that the relative importance of these components varies according to the nature of the criterion used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the four components of the test are not equally valid, reliable, or unique.
the four subtests are valid for their purpose, that they can be combined to form a reliable test, but that the subtests do not contribute equally to test reliability.
the most important criterion for the validation of the components of a foreign language test should be the criterion that best reflects the construct that the test purports to measure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the four components are not equally valid and reliable.
the identification of the major components of English as a language and the validation of these components is an important step in the construction of a test. (Author/JM)
a combination of different criteria is required for the validation of a test, and that a single criterion is not enough for the validation of the test.
